newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand TAB turnover tops NZ$1 billion.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand TAB turnover tops NZ$1 billion.

text.p: The TAB has broken the NZ$1 billion turnover barrier for the first time, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Tuesday.

It has boosted turnover by 11.2 percent to a new record of $1.029 billion in the year until the end of July. This was made up of $995.6 million from racing and $34 million from the first full year of sports betting.
The racing figure is just short of the TAB's target of $1 billion and sports betting surpassed the budgeted figure of $30 million.
TAB general manager George Hickton said he was very happy with the final result.
"We always wanted to get to $1 billion on horse racing but to get so close was still an excellent result," he said.
"When you consider the competition facing the racing industry, you have to be happy with increasing turnover by nearly $200 million in the last two years."
The TAB's profit figures will not be announced until later in the year but Hickton is confident they will exceed the $35.5 million commitment given to the industry.
Hickton said the TAB has set budgets for the new season of $1.05 billion turnover on racing and $40 million on sports betting.
"It is going to be tough to meet those budgets but we have a number of new promotions that will be introduced during the year," he said.

Betting on overseas races and greyhounds have been the significant improvers in the past 12 months. Overseas races have attracted turnover of $177 million, an increase of $49 million or 38.5 percent on the previous year.
Though the TAB has increased the number of races being bet on, overseas racing is now a big contributor to the overall turnover.
It contributed 17.19 percent in the past season compared to 13.82 percent in the 1995-96 season, 7.64 percent in the 1994-95 season and 4.83 percent in the 1993-94 year.
Greyhound racing continues to grow with turnover of $82.2 million, an increase of $20 million or 32.3 percent.
The galloping code produced betting of $471 million which was up $10 million or 2.3 percent, and harness racing dropped by $4.6 million or 1.8 percent to $247 million.

In terms of the total TAB turnover, galloping now provides 45.82 percent (49.82 percent the previous year), harness racing 24.03 percent (27.22 percent), overseas racing 17.19 percent (13.8 percent), greyhounds 7.99 percent (6.71 percent), sport 3.31 percent (0.52 percent) and Pick Six and Six Pack 1.67 percent (1.92 percent).
The greyhound code also showed an increase in turnover on on-course betting, increasing 18.6 percent to $4.3 million.
However, total on-course betting continued its downward trend, dropping by 5.8 percent ($6 million) to $100.5 million.

Galloping attracted $58.9 million, down 4.1 percent, and harness turnover was $37.2 million, down 10.4 percent. On-course betting peaked at $209 million in the 1987-88 season and has been on a downward spiral ever since.
